subject: Pilot availability relief & phased remedy proposal
messages:
From: Amelia Zhang <amelia@horizonai.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@horizonai.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary availability relief during Horizon AI pilot rollout

Hi Priyom,

Quick note from the pilot team at Horizon — we're kicking off our migration of a customer-facing scoring pipeline to Redwood Dedicated next week. The migration includes a short cluster rebalancing window and a staged shard warmup that we expect will temporarily reduce availability for a limited set of production routes.

Can Redwood provide a temporary adjustment to the standard availability target (we typically see 99.95% in the template) for the pilot period (estimated 4–6 weeks) and a reduced remedy/credit profile while we finish the rollout? Our legal/procurement team wants the ask documented so they can approve the pilot POC.

Key constraints:
- Pilot start: 2027-04-18, target end: 2027-05-30 (tentative)
- Required: carveouts for scheduled shard warmup windows and two short blackout windows for data migration (each ~45–60m)
- We want a capped monthly credit during the pilot to limit financial exposure

Attached: high-level rollout calendar from our infra team.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m call if easier.

—Amelia
Amelia Zhang
Head of Platform Engineering, Horizon AI

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Zhang <amelia@horizonai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary availability relief during Horizon AI pilot rollout

Hi Amelia — thanks for the heads up and the calendar. This is a common ask for early Dedicated pilots; I'm confident we can find a pragmatic, documented approach that protects both sides.

Proposal (high level):
- Availability target for pilot period: 99.5% (measured monthly) for the routes affected by the migration.
- Remedy: a phased credit schedule that scales with deviation from the pilot target, capped per calendar month. Example (attached spreadsheet):
  • 99.0%–99.49% => 5% of monthly invoice for affected routes
  • 98.0%–98.99% => 10%
  • <98.0% => 20%
- Monthly cap during pilot: 10% of total monthly Dedicated commitment (this limits exposure while still providing remedy).
- Maintenance carveouts: allow the two planned blackout windows plus an automated maintenance window of up to 2 hours per week for shard warmup during the pilot.
- Measurement: 30-day rolling window aligned to the billing month; outage attribution handled by joint postmortem within 7 business days.

Next steps I suggest: Marissa, can you pull a draft clause we can share with Horizon legal that frames this as a timeboxed pilot amendment to the standard SLA? Ben, please confirm the monthly cap math and whether we want to tie the cap to committed spend or a flat dollar amount.

I've attached a starting remedy table (proposed-remedy-table.xlsx) and our view of the maintenance calendar. If Horizon is comfortable with the principle, we can convert to an amendment and run it through DocuSign.

Happy to refine on a short call — I'm free 11–2 PT tomorrow.

Thanks,
Priyom
Senior Manager, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Amelia Zhang <amelia@horizonai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T12:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary availability relief during Horizon AI pilot rollout

Thanks, Priyom — attaching a short legal-friendly wording snippet that frames the pilot as an "SLA Amendment (Pilot)". Main items to call out in the clause:

1) Timebox: start/end dates with a clause to extend by mutual written agreement.
2) Measurement scope: list of affected routes (we should include the route IDs from Horizon's rollout calendar — Amelia, please paste those when you have a sec).
3) Remedy schedule: mirror Priyom's banding but explicitly call out the monthly cap formula (10% of committed Dedicated spend for the pilot month).
4) Maintenance carveouts: clearly enumerate the two named blackout windows and allow up to 8 maintenance hours per 30-day period that are not eligible for remedy.

Draft snippet (for quick copy into an amendment):
"During the Pilot Term (2027-04-18 through 2027-05-30, unless otherwise extended by mutual written agreement), Redwood will apply the Availability Target of 99.5% for the list of affected Service Routes. Remedy for Availability shortfalls will be applied per the attached phased remedy table and will be capped at 10% of the Customer's monthly Dedicated commitment for the applicable billing period. Scheduled maintenance windows listed in Appendix A and routine shard warmup windows (up to 8 hours per 30-day period) are excluded from Availability calculations"

Ben — if legal is comfortable, Monica should run the final language for procurement acceptance. I've left the measurement and attribution language intentionally simple; we can expand it if Horizon requires more detail.

-Marissa
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Amelia Zhang <amelia@horizonai.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary availability relief during Horizon AI pilot rollout

All — quick commercial note. I'm fine with the 99.5% pilot target and the phased banding, but I recommend the monthly cap be expressed as the lesser of (a) 10% of monthly committed Dedicated spend, or (b) $25,000 for pilot months to keep our exposure bounded on larger deals.

Also recommend we add a requirement that Remedy payouts are net of any credits already provided for separate incident response retainers. Monica, can you confirm whether procurement needs the flat-dollar option included in the amendment?

If Horizon confirms we can accept these two cap options, I'll prepare a short cover email with the amendment to send to Amelia and Carlos and request execution.

Thanks — Ben
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Amelia Zhang <amelia@horizonai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@horizonai.com>
Date: 2027-04-13T16:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary availability relief during Horizon AI pilot rollout

Thanks everyone — Horizon is aligned on the principle. Two quick asks from procurement:

1) Please include the lesser-of cap language Ben suggested (10% or $25k).
2) Add a start/end date and an automatic reversion clause (SLA reverts to standard 99.95% at the earlier of the Pilot End Date or 30 days after completion of migration if not extended).

If you can send a formal amendment with those two edits, we'll route for internal approval. We will sign electronically; please include a DocuSign link if possible and call out the Appendix A maintenance windows so they match our rollout calendar.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Amelia
Head of Platform Engineering, Horizon AI
